h1: Wing Bed — a quiet boutique hotel in the heart of Chiang Mai's Old City, next to Nong Buak Haad Park
intro: Picture this: a small hotel tucked away on Soi Samlan, just 200 metres from Nong Buak Haad Park yet set back from the main road and genuinely quiet, with Wat Phra Singh and Wat Chedi Luang a few minutes' walk away — Wing Bed (now listed on some platforms as The Wing Lanna Hotel) is a boutique hotel inside the Old City that real reviews keep mentioning for the same three things: lovely staff, clean rooms, and a location you can explore on foot all day · It isn't a luxury hotel and there's no pool, but it delivers simple, clean comfort and warm service from about THB 800–1,100/night.

body.html: If you had to sum it up for a friend, Wing Bed is the kind of small boutique hotel you pick for its "location" and its "people" rather than for fancy amenities · It's a three-storey building tucked away on Soi Samlan in Phra Sing, right in the heart of the Chiang Mai Old City (the moat square), only about 200 metres from Nong Buak Haad Park · The appeal here is the simple equation travellers love: you're genuinely inside the Old City, within walking distance of temples and food + clean, simple rooms + staff that many reviews say care more than the price would suggest · It opened back in 2017 and has 25 rooms in total — standard rooms, twin rooms, suites, and family rooms · This is a place built for people who want to use Chiang Mai's Old City as a base: up early for morning alms, temple visits, a cycle around the moat, then back to a clean, quiet room.

The big picture and who it suits — Wing Bed is a great fit for travellers who value staying "genuinely inside the Old City," not just near it · couples or pairs of friends on a modest budget who still want cleanliness and quiet · international visitors coming to Chiang Mai to soak up Lanna culture, walk the temples, take photos, and sit in cafes · and travellers who prefer to get around on foot or by bicycle rather than by car, since this spot is within walking distance of almost every key point inside the moat · Small families can stay too, thanks to the family rooms · As for anyone expecting a pool, a gym, a fancy in-house restaurant, or five-star hotel service, this place may not be the right match — understand from the start that this is a small boutique hotel selling simple cleanliness and friendly service, not a resort or a big chain hotel · One more thing to know: the lane entrance is fairly narrow, so anyone driving a large car or van will want to plan parking ahead.

Location and getting around is where Wing Bed clearly has the edge, because it's genuinely inside the Old City, not on the outskirts · From the hotel it's only about 200 metres to Nong Buak Haad Park (the city-centre park where people like to sit and feed the pigeons) · It's around a 5–7 min walk to Wat Phra Singh, one of the city's most important temples · Wat Chedi Luang is about a 10 min walk away · The Three Kings Monument and the museum quarter are an easy walk · On Sunday nights, the Tha Phae Walking Street (Ratchadamnoen Road) stretches through the heart of the Old City, and Wing Bed is within walking distance — no need to call a ride · If you're flying in, Chiang Mai Airport (CNX) is about 3–4 km away, a 12–15 min drive · It also has a small perk that many reviews praise: being "set back from the main road" makes it quieter than hotels right on a major street, giving you the calm of an Old City lane that's getting harder to find these days.

Rooms and decor — Wing Bed's rooms are around 25–28 square metres, done in a warm minimalist style that leans on cleanliness and ease of use rather than flashy design · Real reviews agree the rooms are "clean and as spacious as they look in the photos," which is high praise given how many places have rooms that turn out smaller than the pictures · Inside you get air conditioning, a 43-inch flat-screen TV, a small fridge, a kettle, and an en-suite bathroom with a rain shower that many guests say is a pleasure to use · The bedding and furniture are good-quality custom pieces, and the bed is just the right amount of soft · The door uses a keycard lock · Overall it's a room that covers all the functions in a size that's just right for staying in the Old City — not cramped, and kept clean.

"Five-star service from the very first minute — the staff did everything to make us feel welcome, the room was clean and spacious just like the photos, and the location made it easy to explore the Old City on foot." — summarised from real reviews on TripAdvisor

Facilities, pool, and spa — Let's be upfront from the start: Wing Bed has no swimming pool and no in-house spa, because it's a small boutique hotel in the Old City with limited space · What it does have is free Wi-Fi throughout the building, a 24-hour reception, luggage storage, laundry service, and a rooftop where you can sit and take in the city — at times used as a quiet corner for meditation or a morning coffee · Parking is available for a fee and should be booked ahead, since space in the Old City is tight · The upside of being a small property is the quiet and the privacy, and as for spa and massage, the Phra Sing area has plenty of good Thai massage shops within walking distance, so it's not an issue for anyone wanting to unwind after a full day of walking · If you want to swim properly, you may need to choose a resort-style stay instead.

Food and bar — One thing that wins over a lot of guests at Wing Bed is breakfast · It's served cooked to order, plate by plate, not a buffet left to keep warm · Real reviews say there are around 5–6 dishes to choose from, including Thai food, bread, cereal, and eggs cooked fresh to order, with one review praising that "the fried egg was cooked just right" and the food was "fresh, made when you order it" — which, for a hotel in this price range, is better than you'd expect · Breakfast is served roughly 7:00–10:00 AM · There's no bar or large restaurant here for lunch and dinner, but the real strength is "the location around you," because the Phra Sing area and the streets around Nong Buak Haad Park are full of northern Thai restaurants, cafes, khao soi shops, and street food — step out of the lane and you'll find affordable local eats, so there's no need to rely on a hotel restaurant at all.

Service is the heart of Wing Bed and the thing most talked about in real reviews · Many guests praise the staff as friendly, smiling, and genuinely helpful — with everything from recommending places to visit, calling rides, and booking tours to looking after the small details that make you feel truly welcomed · Several reviews use the phrase "five-star service in a budget hotel," and some say the staff are the main reason they'd come back · This is where a closely run small boutique hotel often beats a big chain, because warm, friendly hospitality is harder to buy than amenities · For international travellers, the staff speak enough English to handle things smoothly.

Real reviews — the praise · The things mentioned over and over are: (1) the staff are friendly and very helpful, with many ranking this as the standout feature; (2) the rooms are clean and match the photos posted; (3) the Old City location, walkable to temples, the park, and food; (4) the cooked-to-order breakfast is tasty with a choice of dishes; (5) the quiet, calm atmosphere thanks to being set back from the main road · On TripAdvisor this place scores around 4.5 out of 5 from over 160 reviews and ranks near the top of Chiang Mai's guesthouse/small-property category, which reflects that most guests leave impressed — especially with the service and the value.

Real reviews — the gripes · This kind of thing has to be said straight so you can decide · The notes that come up often are: (1) the room walls are fairly thin — some reviews say you can hear conversation or noise from the next room and the hallway, which is common in many small properties in Thailand (there are reports the hotel tried to fix this by carpeting the hallways to cut down on noise); (2) the lane entrance is narrow — anyone driving a large car or van will need to plan parking; (3) some reviews note that the hot water in some bathrooms isn't very steady to adjust and there was once a clogged drain; (4) there's no pool or in-house spa; (5) even though it's in the Old City, some attractions outside the moat still take a 15–20 min drive · All of this is a reasonable trade-off for the price and size of the place, not a problem that leaves most guests disappointed.

Price and value · Room rates at Wing Bed start at about THB 800–1,100/night in normal periods (some overseas platforms show from around 23–25 USD/night for the deluxe and superior rooms) and may climb during high season (November–February), the Yi Peng/Loy Krathong festival, Songkran, or weekends when the Walking Street is on · Compared with other Old City stays at similar prices, where Wing Bed wins is that you get a clean, well-sized room, cooked-to-order breakfast, and warmer-than-the-price service, in a central Old City location you can explore on foot · For travellers who value location and service over resort-style amenities, the value here is very good against the alternatives in the same area · Book in low season or far ahead and you've a good chance of an even better rate.

Good to know before you book · This is a small boutique hotel with only 25 rooms, and during high season and festivals it fills up very fast, so book ahead · If you're sensitive to noise, ask for a room away from the hallway or on the top floor to reduce noise from neighbouring rooms · If you're driving, ask about parking and the width of the lane entrance ahead of time, since the lane is fairly narrow · Note that some platforms now show the hotel name as "The Wing Lanna Hotel" (it used to be called WING BED) — the same address is 85 Samlarn Road, Phra Sing, so search using both names side by side · It's worth choosing a Free Cancellation option if your plans aren't firm yet · And if you're arriving late, let them know your check-in time ahead of time, even though reception is open 24 hours.

How to book · Wing Bed / The Wing Lanna Hotel is on all the major platforms — Agoda, Booking.com, Trip.com, and TripAdvisor · Prices can differ quite a bit between periods and platforms, so it's worth comparing several before you book · The booking links below go directly to the hotel page where possible; on platforms where the hotel name might overlap with another "The Wing" in Chiang Mai, search with the name plus the address "85 Samlarn Road Phra Sing" to be sure it's the right hotel · You can also book direct via the website wingbed.com, the WINGBED Facebook page, or by phone at 053-275858 / 098-562-3558, which can sometimes get you more flexible terms.

The bottom line · Wing Bed isn't for anyone after a pool, a spa, or five-star hotel service · But if you're looking for a clean, quiet stay with cooked-to-order breakfast and warm staff, in a central Old City location walkable to Wat Phra Singh, Wat Chedi Luang, Nong Buak Haad Park, and the Walking Street, for the high hundreds to low thousands of baht — this is one of the best value picks in the Phra Sing area · Real reviews all point the same way: the standouts are the "people" and the "location," with small trade-offs like fairly thin walls, a narrow lane entrance, and no pool · If you can live with those limits, Wing Bed is a very good base for exploring Chiang Mai's Old City on a budget while getting a genuinely local feel.

faqTitle: Frequently asked questions — Wing Bed Chiang Mai

faq.q: Where is Wing Bed in Chiang Mai · what's nearby?
faq.a: Wing Bed is at 85 Soi Samlan, Samlarn Road, Phra Sing, inside the Old City (the moat square) · It's about 200 metres from Nong Buak Haad Park · a 5–7 min walk to Wat Phra Singh · 10 min to Wat Chedi Luang · 10–15 min to the Sunday Walking Street · about 3–4 km from Chiang Mai Airport, a 12–15 min drive.

faq.q: What does Wing Bed cost to start · what rooms are there?
faq.a: Rates start at about THB 800–1,100/night in normal periods (some platforms show from around 23–25 USD/night) · There are Standard, Superior/Twin, Suite, and Family rooms — 25 in total · Prices climb in high season (Nov–Feb) and during festivals, so it's worth comparing several platforms before booking.

faq.q: Who is Wing Bed best for?
faq.a: It's a great fit for couples, pairs of friends, or travellers who want to stay genuinely in the Old City and explore temples and food on foot · There's a family room for small families · It's not a good fit for anyone wanting a pool, a spa, or big-hotel service.

faq.q: Does Wing Bed have a pool or breakfast?
faq.a: No swimming pool, but there is cooked-to-order breakfast served plate by plate, with a choice of 5–6 dishes including eggs cooked fresh to order, around 7:00–10:00 AM — something many reviews praise · There's also free Wi-Fi, a rooftop to relax on, and a 24-hour reception.

faq.q: What do real reviews praise and criticise?
faq.a: Praise: friendly, very helpful staff (the standout feature), clean rooms matching the photos, a central Old City location, cooked-to-order breakfast, and a quiet, calm atmosphere · Gripes: fairly thin room walls so you hear the next room, a narrow lane entrance, unsteady hot water in some rooms, and no pool/spa.

faq.q: Are Wing Bed and The Wing Lanna Hotel the same place?
faq.a: It's the same address · Some platforms now show the hotel name as The Wing Lanna Hotel (formerly WING BED), at the same address of 85 Samlarn Road, Phra Sing · When searching, use both names plus the address to be sure it's the right hotel, because Chiang Mai has several places whose names start with The Wing.
